name: crc-fast (SIMD CRC-16/32/64 for all catalogued variants)
baseline: crc crate 3.x with its default bytewise table (about 0.5 GiB/s)
verdict_reason: The '>220X' headline pairs the best row (about 111 GiB/s for CRC-32/ISCSI on 1 MiB inputs with AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ on Sapphire Rapids) with the crc crate's default bytewise table measured elsewhere. On 1 KiB inputs the same machine shows about 61 GiB/s, Graviton2 reaches about 17 GiB/s at 1 MiB, and crc's own Slice16 option does 3.30 GiB/s, so against a tuned software CRC the gain is roughly 5x to 34x (derived from page data), not 220x.
tier_reason: CPU and SIMD target are stated per row, but the 220x comparison uses a crc figure from another machine, values are rounded, and no rustc version or command is given.
claimed_speedup: Up to >220X faster than the crc crate at ~0.5GiB/s; CRC-32/ISCSI ~111 GiB/s (1 MiB) and ~61 GiB/s (1 KiB) on Sapphire Rapids with avx512-vpclmulqdq; CRC-32/ISO-HDLC ~88 GiB/s (1 MiB); Graviton2 ~17 GiB/s (1 MiB); crc's Slice16 is 3.30 GiB/s on a Ryzen 7 3800X.
workload: CRC-32/ISCSI, CRC-32/ISO-HDLC, CRC-64/NVME and forward variants over 1 KiB and 1 MiB buffers.
hardware: Intel Sapphire Rapids (EC2 c7i.metal-24xl), AMD Genoa (EC2 c7a.metal-48xl), AWS Graviton4 and Graviton2, Apple M3 Ultra, Apple M4 Max
platforms: aarch64, x86_64 and x86 SIMD; table-based fallback elsewhere; C-compatible library
one_liner: SIMD CRC for every CRC-16/32/64 variant, reaching ~111 GiB/s on AVX-512 servers; the '>220X' headline compares against crc's slowest default.
how_it_is_fast: It generalizes Intel's PCLMULQDQ folding method to any Rocksoft-model polynomial, folding 1 MiB inputs with VPCLMULQDQ on 512-bit registers or PMULL on ARM. For CRC-32/ISCSI and, on aarch64, CRC-32/ISO-HDLC it fuses carry-less multiply folding with the CPU's native CRC instructions.
use_it_when: CRC-64/NVME (S3 checksums), CRC-32C or uncommon CRC variants that crc32fast does not cover
Large buffers on AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ servers or recent ARM cores
skip_it_when: Small inputs where call overhead dominates
caveats: x86 rows are all AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ server CPUs; older x86 without VPCLMULQDQ is not shown
No head-to-head with crc32fast or crc32c on the same machine
